Screen facet combinations for departures from a fitted model

Source: R/api-tables.R, R/api-estimation.R, R/api-methods.R, and 1 more
estimate_bias.Rd

Estimate conditional plug-in interaction shifts \(b_{jc}\) within [-max_abs, max_abs] holding a fitted RSM, PCM, or one-family GPCM baseline calibration and Person measures fixed (FACETS Table 13 screen; for jointly estimated interactions use facet_interactions in fit_mfrm() and mfrm_facet_intervals()).

interaction_effect_table() returns the fixed-effect interaction block estimated by fit_mfrm() when facet_interactions is supplied. These are model-estimated deviations from the additive main-effects MFRM, not the residual screening statistics returned by estimate_bias().

Usage

estimate_bias(
  fit,
  diagnostics,
  facet_a = NULL,
  facet_b = NULL,
  interaction_facets = NULL,
  max_abs = 10,
  omit_extreme = TRUE,
  max_iter = 4,
  tol = 0.001,
  xtreme = 0
)

interaction_effect_table(fit, comparison_review = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_bias'
summary(object, digits = 3, top_n = 10, p_cut = 0.05, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_bias'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("scatter", "ranked", "heatmap", "abs_t_hist", "facet_profile"),
  ...
)

bias_count_table(
  bias_results,
  min_count_warn = 10,
  branch = c("original", "facets"),
  fit = NULL
)

Arguments

fit

Optional fit_mfrm() result used to attach run context metadata.

diagnostics

Matching fit_mfrm() and diagnose_mfrm() outputs.

facet_a

Two facet names (facet_a, facet_b) or a character vector of >= 2 facets (interaction_facets supports 3+ way screens and explicit "Person" plug-in screens).

facet_b

Two facet names (facet_a, facet_b) or a character vector of >= 2 facets (interaction_facets supports 3+ way screens and explicit "Person" plug-in screens).

interaction_facets

Two facet names (facet_a, facet_b) or a character vector of >= 2 facets (interaction_facets supports 3+ way screens and explicit "Person" plug-in screens).

max_abs

Search bound on |Bias Size|, extreme-element exclusion toggle, iteration-pass log ceiling and tolerance, and optional inward extreme-cell total adjustment (0 default withholds boundary SE/tails; .5 gives BiasStatus = "extreme_adjusted" in additive RSM/PCM JML without group anchors).

omit_extreme

Search bound on |Bias Size|, extreme-element exclusion toggle, iteration-pass log ceiling and tolerance, and optional inward extreme-cell total adjustment (0 default withholds boundary SE/tails; .5 gives BiasStatus = "extreme_adjusted" in additive RSM/PCM JML without group anchors).

max_iter

Search bound on |Bias Size|, extreme-element exclusion toggle, iteration-pass log ceiling and tolerance, and optional inward extreme-cell total adjustment (0 default withholds boundary SE/tails; .5 gives BiasStatus = "extreme_adjusted" in additive RSM/PCM JML without group anchors).

tol

Search bound on |Bias Size|, extreme-element exclusion toggle, iteration-pass log ceiling and tolerance, and optional inward extreme-cell total adjustment (0 default withholds boundary SE/tails; .5 gives BiasStatus = "extreme_adjusted" in additive RSM/PCM JML without group anchors).

xtreme

Search bound on |Bias Size|, extreme-element exclusion toggle, iteration-pass log ceiling and tolerance, and optional inward extreme-cell total adjustment (0 default withholds boundary SE/tails; .5 gives BiasStatus = "extreme_adjusted" in additive RSM/PCM JML without group anchors).

comparison_review

Optional result of describe_mfrm_data() with comparisons, or its $comparison_review component. Returns the declared interaction contrasts from a matching joint fit instead of individual cells.

object

Output from estimate_bias().

digits

Number of digits for printed numeric values.

top_n

Number of strongest bias rows to keep.

p_cut

Tail-area cutoff used for counting screen-positive rows.

...

For plot(): Named controls below. draw = FALSE returns the plot data without drawing. Controls do not change the fitted calibration.

For summary(): Reserved for generic compatibility.

x

A result from estimate_bias().

type

"scatter", "ranked", "heatmap", "abs_t_hist", or "facet_profile".

bias_results

Output from estimate_bias().

min_count_warn

Minimum count threshold for flagging sparse bias cells.

branch

Output branch: "facets" keeps legacy manual-aligned naming, "original" returns compact QC-oriented names.

Value

An mfrm_bias list with table, summary, chi_sq, interaction_facets, iteration, orientation_review, mixed_sign, direction_note, recommended_action, inference_tier, and optimization_failures.

A tibble with one row per interaction cell. Returns an empty tibble when the fit has no model-estimated facet interactions. With comparison_review, one row per requested contrast with availability, numerical and readiness fields; attributes comparison_review, fit_checks and notes preserve the prospective question, source fingerprint and numerical evidence, and interpretation limits.

For summary(): An object of class summary.mfrm_bias with:

  • overview: interaction facets/order, cell counts, and effect-size profile

  • chi_sq: fixed-effect chi-square block

  • final_iteration: end-of-iteration status row

  • top_rows: highest-|t| interaction rows

  • notes: short interpretation notes

For plot(): Invisibly, a ggplot object carrying view-specific tables, retained screening rules and interpretation notes accessible via plot_data(). Plot agreement across views is not independent evidence of bias. Use plot_data(p, "notes") for the interaction definition, score-direction caveat, magnitude-only facet-profile interpretation and conditional uncertainty qualifications outside the figure.

A named list with:

  • table: cell-level counts with low-count flags

  • by_facet: named list of counts aggregated by each interaction facet

  • by_facet_a, by_facet_b: first two facet summaries (legacy compatibility)

  • summary: one-row summary

  • thresholds: applied thresholds

  • branch, style: output branch metadata

  • fit_overview: optional one-row fit metadata when fit is supplied

Details

For additive predictor \(\eta_{njc} = \theta_n - \delta_j - \beta_c + b_{jc}\), interior solutions solve \(\sum_n w_{njc}\{X_{njc} - E_{njc}(b_{jc})\} = 0\) with conditional SE \([\sum_n w_{njc}\mathrm{Var}_{njc}(\hat b)]^{-1/2}\) (including slope factors and conditional LR/profile columns in one-family GPCM). Screening t tails use continuous Student df = weighted_count - 1 (ProbabilityStatus, ScreenStatus); calibration uncertainty is not propagated.

mfrmr supports two-way interactions between non-person facets, for example facet_interactions = "Rater:Criterion". Each interaction matrix is identified by zero marginal sums across both participating facets, so the interaction estimates are separable from the two main effects. Positive values indicate higher-than-expected scores for the facet-level combination under the additive model; negative values indicate lower-than-expected scores.

Use this table for confirmatory model review after specifying the facet pair of substantive interest. For exploratory screening without adding parameters to the fitted model, use estimate_bias() or estimate_all_bias().

With comparison_review, first fit the declared model using the review's fit_arguments and the original ratings. The fit must match the retained responses, origins, score coding, model, constraints, facet orientation, step owner and population design. Only native, unadjusted RSM/PCM fits without shrinkage are supported. The contrast is the declared weighted sum of Group1-minus-Group2 interaction effects, in logits. Positive means a relative shift toward higher coded scores; it is not an absolute school effect or evidence of unfairness. Location and step effects are not added.

This route reevaluates the retained likelihood and full gradient without optimization. Objective agreement must be within 1e-6 and the gradient sup norm within max(1e-4, 10 * reltol), matching the ordinary numerical stopping tolerance. For MML it also evaluates 2 * q + 1 quadrature nodes, requiring the finer-grid gradient to meet that tolerance and the absolute negative-log-likelihood change per Person to be at most 1e-6. These are numerical checks, not statistical precision criteria. A failed check retains the row with Estimate = NA and an explanation; the separate OptimizerEstimate is a diagnostic trace. No refit or partial fit is run.

EstimateStatus = "descriptive_only" requires full conditional-map rank, numerical convergence, current readiness information and no recorded blocking condition or boundary exclusion. It does not certify finite-MLE existence, global marginal identification or sampling performance. MML retains State = "not_evaluated" for positive conditional ranks even when a descriptive fitted contrast is available. BoundaryState, FitReadiness, NumericalState and QuadratureState remain separate. SE, Lower, Upper remain missing and FormalInferenceEligible remains false. A target-only identified contrast in a rejected full model remains unavailable through this route. Save the returned table with saveRDS() to preserve its review and checks without recalculation; CSV retains the visible columns but not the attributes.

For a mfrm_comparison_fit created with fit_scope = "comparisons", omit comparison_review: the table already contains the declared targets and their partial-fit checks. Extraction does not fit again. See fit_mfrm_technical_details for its likelihood-preserving parameterization, availability requirements and limits. For full RSM/PCM MML fits, mfrm_facet_intervals() with the same comparison_review separately supplies model-information intervals and supported population-SD standardization; extraction here stays descriptive. CML comparison fits add conditional-information SEs and pointwise 95 percent Wald limits for identified targets, with conditional_wald status; unidentified rows remain missing. The ordinary full-fit route above remains unchanged.

summary() collects cell availability, magnitudes and conditional screening results from a saved bias analysis.

For summary(): Read overview, the conditional all-zero chi_sq screen and final_iteration; top_rows ranks absolute t and retains GPCM profile columns when present. These reuse the screening qualifications above, not a formal bias test. Use mfrm_report_bias_interaction for detailed review.

plot() method: Plot saved bias-interaction results

Inspect the pattern of conditional interaction estimates from estimate_bias(). Start with ranked interactions, then use other views to understand the pattern.

For plot(): Visualization front-end for mfrm_report_bias_interaction with multiple views. With draw = FALSE, plot_data(p) includes plot_long, plot_annotations, flag_summary, and plot_settings in addition to the view-specific ranked_table, scatter_data, facet_profile, and heatmap components. Use these fields when rebuilding the same screening view in plotly, Quarto, or a dashboard. Saved report thresholds determine flags, reference lines and returned notes; recreate mfrm_report_bias_interaction from the saved bias object to change them. Scatter views attach aligned marginal histograms when marginal = "auto" (with \(n \ge 8\)) or "histogram". Conditional bounds and their status remain separate from calibration-inclusive uncertainty.

This helper summarizes how many observations contribute to each bias-cell estimate and flags sparse cells.

Branch behavior:

  • "facets": keeps legacy manual-aligned column labels (Sq, Observd Count, Obs-Exp Average, Model S.E.) for side-by-side comparison with external workflows.

  • "original": keeps compact field names (Count, BiasSize, SE) for custom QC workflows and scripting.

References

  • Linacre, J. M. (1989). Many-Facet Rasch Measurement. MESA Press. (FACETS Table 13 corresponds to the bias / interaction estimation that this helper implements.)

  • Eckes, T. (2005). Examining rater effects in TestDaF writing and speaking performance assessments: A many-facet Rasch analysis. Language Assessment Quarterly, 2(3), 197-221.

  • Eckes, T. (2015). Introduction to many-facet Rasch measurement: Analyzing and evaluating rater-mediated assessments (2nd ed.). Peter Lang.

  • Myford, C. M., & Wolfe, E. W. (2003). Detecting and measuring rater effects using many-facet Rasch measurement: Part I. Journal of Applied Measurement, 4(4), 386-422.

  • Myford, C. M., & Wolfe, E. W. (2004). Detecting and measuring rater effects using many-facet Rasch measurement: Part II. Journal of Applied Measurement, 5(2), 189-227.

Controls

For plot():

  • facet_a, facet_b, or interaction_facets identify the interaction; top_n = 40 and sort_by = "abs_t" ("abs_bias" or "prob" also accepted) select ranked interactions.

  • abs_t_warn = 2, abs_bias_warn = 0.5, and p_max = 0.05 set screening rules when preparing a report from the bias result. They are review aids, not guarantees of a calibrated error rate.

  • show_ci = FALSE omits whiskers; ci_level = 0.95 chooses their level for scatter/ranked views. GPCM rows retain conditional profile bounds, with dashed whiskers for search-limited or unverified bounds. Other rows use conditional per-cell SEs. Missing profile bounds are not replaced with another method. These intervals omit calibration uncertainty; endpoint completion is not evidence of coverage.

  • preset selects "standard", "publication", "compact", or "monochrome"; palette overrides named colors (normal, flag, hist, profile); label_angle controls label rotation. title sets title metadata (main is a compatibility alias; supply only one).

Plot types

"scatter" (default)

Observed-minus-expected score average (x) versus conditional bias size in logits (y). Points use the saved flag status; horizontal guides show the saved absolute-bias threshold and zero, with a vertical guide at zero score difference.

"ranked"

Conditional bias size (x) for up to top_n saved ranked interactions (y). Points are colored by flag status; optional whiskers retain the conditional uncertainty and incomplete-bound status. A saved report retains the ranking chosen when it was constructed.

"heatmap"

Facet A by facet B matrix of signed bias size. Cells retain reusable matrix and flag tables for dashboards. This is a Table 13 follow-up display: it supports pattern recognition but does not turn screening rows into confirmatory tests.

"abs_t_hist"

Histogram of absolute screening t-statistics across all interaction cells. Dashed reference line at abs_t_warn. Use for assessing the overall distribution of interaction effect sizes.

"facet_profile"

Per-facet-level aggregation showing mean absolute bias and flag rate. Useful for identifying which individual facet levels drive systematic interaction patterns.

Reading bias plots

Use scatter/ranked views to locate cells, then histogram/facet profiles for pattern summaries. They reuse the same estimates and flags, not independent evidence. Review exposure, calibration uncertainty and substantive explanations.

Interpreting output

  • table: cell-level contribution counts and low-count flags.

  • by_facet: sparse-cell structure by each interaction facet.

  • summary: overall low-count prevalence.

  • fit_overview: optional run context (when fit is supplied).

Low-count cells should be interpreted cautiously because bias-size estimates can become unstable with sparse support.

Typical workflow

  1. Estimate bias with estimate_bias().

  2. Build bias_count_table(...) in desired branch.

  3. Review low-count flags before interpreting bias magnitudes.

Further guidance

For a plot-selection guide and a longer walkthrough, see mfrmr_visual_diagnostics and vignette("mfrmr-visual-diagnostics", package = "mfrmr").

Output columns

The table data.frame contains, in the legacy-compatible branch:

FacetA, FacetB

Interaction facet level identifiers; generic names for the two interaction facets.

Sq

Sequential row number.

Observd Count

Number of observations for this cell.

Obs-Exp Average

Observed minus expected average for this cell.

Model S.E.

Standard error of the bias estimate.

Infit, Outfit

Fit statistics for this cell.

LowCountFlag

Logical; TRUE when count < min_count_warn.

The summary data.frame contains:

InteractionFacets

Names of the interaction facets.

Cells, TotalCount

Number of cells and total observations.

LowCountCells, LowCountPercent

Number and share of low-count cells.

Examples

# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("estimate_bias", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Saved synthetic JML/RSM analysis of example_bias.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "bias-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit
diag <- example_fit$diagnostics
bias <- estimate_bias(fit, diag, facet_a = "Rater", facet_b = "Criterion", max_iter = 2)
s_bias <- summary(bias)
s_bias$overview
# This example uses the default RSM, so Bias Size is also in logit units.
# `Significant` counts cells crossing the screening rule, not proven bias.
# The `BonferroniSignificant` /
#   `HolmSignificant` columns count cells that survive multiple-
#   testing adjustment to screening tail areas. Zero flags do not
#   establish absence of bias or equivalence.
s_bias$top_rows
# An illustrative review rule is |t| > 2 and |Bias Size| > 0.5 logits.
# Choose the effect threshold substantively; these cutoffs do not
#   establish statistical reliability;
#   inspect cell counts, uncertainty and substantive consequences.
p_bias <- plot(bias, type = "bias", draw = FALSE)
plot_data(p_bias, "plot")
# Optional finite reporting for extreme cells; this does not refit calibration
extreme_bias <- estimate_bias(fit, diag, "Rater", "Criterion", xtreme = .5)
head(extreme_bias$table[, c("Bias Size", "PrimaryBias", "BiasStatus", "SEBasis")])

} # }
# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("interaction_effect_table", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
toy <- load_mfrmr_data("example_operational")
fit <- fit_mfrm(
  toy, person = "Person", facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score", method = "MML", model = "RSM",
  facet_interactions = "Rater:Criterion",
  quad_points = 7, maxit = 30
)
head(interaction_effect_table(fit))
} # }
# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("summary.mfrm_bias", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
toy <- load_mfrmr_data("example_bias")
toy <- toy[toy$Person %in% unique(toy$Person)[1:8], ]
fit <- fit_mfrm(toy, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score", method = "JML", maxit = 30)
diag <- diagnose_mfrm(fit, residual_pca = "none")
bias <- estimate_bias(fit, diag, facet_a = "Rater", facet_b = "Criterion", max_iter = 1)
summary(bias)
} # }
# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("plot.mfrm_bias", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Saved synthetic JML/RSM analysis of example_bias.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "bias-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit
diagnostics <- example_fit$diagnostics
bias <- estimate_bias(fit, diagnostics = diagnostics,
  facet_a = "Rater", facet_b = "Criterion")
p <- plot(bias, type = "ranked", preset = "publication", draw = FALSE)
head(plot_data(p, "ranked_table"))
} # }
# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("bias_count_table", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Saved synthetic JML/RSM analysis of example_bias.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "bias-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit
diag <- example_fit$diagnostics
bias <- estimate_bias(fit, diag, facet_a = "Rater", facet_b = "Criterion", max_iter = 2)
t11 <- bias_count_table(bias)
t11_facets <- bias_count_table(bias, branch = "facets", fit = fit)
summary(t11)
p <- plot(t11, draw = FALSE)
p2 <- plot(t11, type = "lowcount_by_facet", draw = FALSE)
if (interactive()) {
  plot(
    t11,
    type = "cell_counts",
    draw = TRUE,
    main = "Bias Cell Counts (Customized)",
    palette = c(count = "#2b8cbe", low = "#cb181d"),
    label_angle = 45
  )
}
} # }
